title: The foundry listers drop an unreadable run.json and the feed prunes the run
body:
## Summary
listRuns, listExtractRuns, listCycles and listStripRuns discard listManifests' warnings, so a run whose run.json is unreadable vanishes from the feed's read with no skipped line and the sync prunes every item of that run.

## Description
lib/foundry/runStore.ts:107 listManifests returns `{ items, warnings }` and logs each warning; lib/foundry/store.ts:100 (listRuns), lib/foundry/extract/store.ts:210, lib/foundry/training/store.ts:120 and lib/foundry/strips/store.ts:169 destructure only `items`. The run feeds (lib/library/feeds/foundry.ts) therefore see a clean, shorter list, and lib/library/project.ts prunes the run as gone - the data-access honesty contract's silently short list that a consumer acts on. 2f5717ae added FeedRead.held for a run the feed listed and could not read; this is the same case one level lower, where the feed never sees the run at all. Fixed: each lister returns (or exposes) its warnings; the four feeds push them to `skipped` and their id prefixes to `held`.

## Flow
- sync once with a strips run whose run.json is valid (1 item inserted)
- overwrite run.json with '{ torn'
- sync again: report {items 0, pruned 1, skipped []}; the poster is gone from the index
- fix: listers surface warnings -> feed skipped names the run, held keeps its items, pruned 0

## Expected impact
An operator whose run manifest is damaged sees the run's plates vanish from the Library with no reason anywhere but a console line. Changing the listers' return shape touches their other callers (the Foundry screens).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an unreadable run manifest neither prunes its items nor goes unreported
Before: probe 2026-10-25 (temp STRIPS_STORE_DIR, in-memory kernel): second sync {items 0, pruned 1, skipped []}
After: predicted {pruned 0, skipped [run id]} once the lister's warnings reach the feed
Method: probe - Before measured; the fix lives in lib/foundry/* (four listers outside this context's paths)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: tests/next-server/library-feeds.test.ts case: strips run synced clean, then run.json overwritten with '{ torn', second sync asserts pruned 0 and skipped names the run; seed red on the current tree (pruned 1, skipped [])

title: The scout feed skips an unreadable night and then prunes its items
body:
## Summary
lib/library/feeds/scout.ts reads each committed night and, when readNight throws, reports it in skipped and continues - so the sync prunes every item of that night, the shape 2f5717ae fixed in the four run feeds.

## Description
lib/library/feeds/scout.ts:100-104 `catch (e) { skipped.push({ id: summary.id, reason: errorMessage(e) }); continue; }` with no `held` prefix; lib/library/project.ts then prunes against the shorter read. The same file slices listNights() to NIGHT_CAP (lib/library/feeds/scout.ts:97) without a skipped line, the cap 915cf884 made visible in the run feeds. The file is the operator's concurrent feature work and is not in this context's file_paths, so it was not touched. Fixed: push the night's item-id prefixes to `held` on the read failure, and report the cap.

## Flow
- sync with a committed night (its items inserted)
- make readNight throw for it (torn night file)
- sync again: items pruned, the night only in skipped

## Expected impact
Kept scout scenes leave the Library whenever a night file is unreadable. Low risk: an optional FeedRead field the sync already honours.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - an unreadable night keeps its items
Before: simulation - the catch at scout.ts:102 is the same shape the strips probe measured at pruned 1 before 2f5717ae
After: predicted pruned 0 with held prefixes
Method: simulation - the file is a foreign session's in-flight feature file (veto 4), not probed here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a scout-feed case in tests/next-server (temp scout store): sync a committed night, tear its file, sync again; assert pruned 0 and skipped names it; seed red on the current scout.ts

title: The sync buffers each ingested file whole in memory before hashing it
body:
## Summary
lib/library/project.ts ingest() reads a file with readFile into one Uint8Array and hands it to BlobStore.put, so an export or music-video mp4 of hundreds of MB is held whole in the sync's process (inside the Next server when freshLibrary runs).

## Description
lib/library/project.ts ingest: `bytes = new Uint8Array(await readFile(file.abs)); const ref = await blobs.put(bytes, file.mime);`; packages/kernel/src/blob.ts:33 `put(bytes: Uint8Array, mime: string)` has no streaming variant. The exports and mv feeds point at finished cuts (lib/library/feeds/studio.ts, sound.ts mvFeed). A stream put (hash while copying to the blob dir) would bound memory at a chunk. The kernel blob API is outside this context.

## Flow
- export a 1080p cut (hundreds of MB)
- visit the Library: freshLibrary starts a sync in the server process
- ingest reads the whole mp4 into one buffer, then put hashes and writes it

## Expected impact
Server memory rises by the size of the largest new file per sync. Changing BlobStore is a kernel seam with other callers.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - ingest memory bounded by a chunk, not by the file
Before: not measured - predicted peak RSS rise ~= file size (readFile)
After: predicted ~= stream chunk size
Method: simulation - an RSS probe over a 512 MB temp file on both arms is the instrument; the change is in packages/kernel/src/blob.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: script: write a 512 MB temp file, run syncLibrary over a one-item feed with a temp blob dir and in-memory kernel, sample process.memoryUsage().rss peak; both arms
drain_note: trade-off for the operator: memory vs re-ingest cost; reverted

title: The ledger's syncSoon leaves its claim open when a sync throws
body:
## Summary
lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts syncSoon has the catch abb6aa95 fixed in the Library: a sync that rejects past its report logs and leaves the ledger-sync claim open until its TTL.

## Description
lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:287-293 closes the claim in `.then` only; `.catch` logs `[ledger-sync] failed outside its own report`. The two syncSoon twins (lib/library/project.ts syncLibrarySoon, now fixed) now disagree. Fixed: the same finishClaim(..., { error }) in the catch.

## Flow
- make a source's mapping throw outside its own read
- syncSoon: claim stays open, next sync waits the TTL
- fix: claim closed with the error as report

## Expected impact
The Ledger's background sync recovers at its interval after a crash instead of the TTL.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a crashed ledger sync closes its claim
Before: simulation - identical code shape to the library twin, which measured finished_at null before abb6aa95
After: predicted finished_at set
Method: simulation - out of this context's paths (ledger-v1-projection-core)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: lib/ledger/v1/sync.ts:293  .catch((e: unknown) => console.error(`[ledger-sync] failed outside its own report: ${errorMessage(e)}`));
instrument: tests/next-server ledger sync case mirroring library-sync's 'closes the claim with the error' (a store/source that throws outside its read); seed red on HEAD

title: blobRootFor is a second copy of kernelProcess's blobRootOf
body:
## Summary
lib/library/fresh.ts blobRootFor re-implements lib/kernelProcess.ts blobRootOf expression for expression, keyed on a location string instead of a Store.

## Description
lib/library/fresh.ts:35 and lib/kernelProcess.ts:47 both read `location === ":memory:" ? path.resolve(OUT_DIRNAME, "blobs") : path.join(path.dirname(location), "blobs")`. freshLibrary could call blobRootOf(store) directly, but pipeline/library-sync.mts needs the string form, and blobRootOf takes a whole Store. Fixed: blobRootOf takes `Pick<Store, "location">`, blobRootFor goes, both callers use the one rule.

## Flow
- grep the expression: 2 definitions
- fix: 1 definition, 2 callers

## Expected impact
A change to where in-memory kernels keep blobs lands in one place. Touches lib/kernelProcess.ts (outside this context).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the blob-root rule
Before: 2 definitions (fresh.ts:35, kernelProcess.ts:47)
After: 1
Method: probe - the grep count; the fix needs lib/kernelProcess.ts's signature widened
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/library/fresh.ts:35  export const blobRootFor = (location: string): string => (location === ":memory:" ? path.resolve(OUT_DIRNAME, "blobs") : path.join(path.dirname(location), "blobs"));
lib/kernelProcess.ts:47  export const blobRootOf = (store: Store): string => (store.location === ":memory:" ? path.resolve(OUT_DIRNAME, "blobs") : path.join(path.dirname(store.location), "blobs"));
instrument: grep count of the ':memory:' blob-root expression across lib/ (2 -> 1) plus typecheck green

title: Runs past the newest 200 leave the Library: hold their items or let them go
body:
## Summary
The four run feeds read only the newest 200 runs, so once a store passes 200 the oldest runs' items - kept plates included - are pruned from the Library; 915cf884 made the cap visible but did not change what it does.

## Description
lib/library/feeds/foundry.ts newest() slices to RUN_CAP = 200 and now reports the remainder; lib/library/project.ts prunes the unread runs' items. The context's description says the Library indexes everything the studio has made. Holding them is a few lines (push the past-cap runs' prefixes to FeedRead.held, as 2f5717ae does for an unreadable run), but a held item is then frozen - a deleted old run's items would never prune - so whether the Library is bounded by the read cap or keeps the long tail is a product call.

## Flow
- store reaches 201 forge runs
- sync: the oldest run's plates are pruned; skipped says 1 of 201 runs are not read
- option A (today): bounded index; option B: held, frozen, never pruned

## Expected impact
Today extract has 37 runs and forge 0, so neither arm bites yet.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - what the Library holds past the read cap
Before: past-cap runs pruned (reported since 915cf884)
After: a decision, not a figure
Method: simulation - both arms are a few lines; the choice is what the Library is for
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
lib/library/feeds/foundry.ts  const RUN_CAP = 200;  newest(): return all.slice(0, RUN_CAP);
foundry-out run dirs 2026-10-25: extract 37, runs 0, strips 0, training 0
